A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMG research, with matching architecture, core experiments and per-scene results. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original OMG rendering, compression, timing and ablation results on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks&Temples and Deep Blending, including per-scene and compression analyses in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds quantization comparisons, MCMC integration, Zip-NeRF evaluation, sparse-baseline experiments, neighbor-search comparisons and lower-end GPU measurements.

M1.justification: The architecture, SVQ procedure and training objective remain intact. Equation (8) changes the stated local-distinctiveness score normalization from 1/K, the neighbor count, to 1/D, the feature dimension. This is a limited scoring-formula revision, without evidence of different pruning decisions. The generalized feature notation still uses D=3 in the documented original setup.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on the larger, more complex scenes of the Zip-NeRF dataset (Table 7 and Section 5), extending coverage to a regime where the original baseline densification becomes inadequate. All three original datasets and their per-scene coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The comparison set expands substantially: Mini-Splatting joins Tables 1–3, LocoGS-L is added to the Tanks&Temples and Deep Blending comparison, and RVQ joins the quantization comparison. New experiments evaluate 3DGS-MCMC, Zip-NeRF and SMERF, plus Mini-Splatting combinations with Compact-3DGS and LocoGS. These are reported comparisons, not citation-only additions.

E3.justification: New protocols include MCMC evaluations at 500K/1M Gaussians, Zip-NeRF training with 3M Gaussians for 150K iterations, COLMAP-initialized LocoGS comparisons and GTX 1080 Ti timing. The VQ comparison changes appearance codebooks from 2^13 to 2^14 entries, expands to three OMG sizes and reports codebook-initialization time instead of total training time. The original OMG training schedule remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds LD scoring without attribute compression (Figure 5), removal of SVQ (Table 4), RVQ and expanded VQ comparisons (Table 5), and transfer to MCMC (Table 6). Appendices A–C additionally test competing compressors with sparse Gaussians, Morton-order approximation against KNN, and rendering on weaker hardware. These substantially extend the questions tested beyond v1's ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of error bars but introduces no statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Original OMG benchmark and per-scene values are retained, but substantial new results are added. Examples include MCMC+OMG achieving 26.69 PSNR at 29.0 MB on Zip-NeRF and OMG-XS rendering at 106 FPS versus LocoGS's 73 FPS on GTX 1080 Ti. Table 5 replaces the VQ-XS result of 26.97 PSNR/3.99 MB with 27.06/4.21 under revised codebooks, not a same-setting gain. Figure 4 also uses different views and results.

T1.justification: Equation (8) revises the mathematical definition of the LD score by replacing normalization by K with normalization by D. The remaining rendering and quantization equations are retained. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and none are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: compact sparse-Gaussian representation, SVQ and local-distinctiveness pruning. The headline claims of approximately 49–50% storage reduction, approximately 4.1 MB on Mip-NeRF 360 and 600+ FPS are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 5 explicitly bounds OMG by its underlying densification method, explains failures on large Zip-NeRF scenes and discusses integration with MCMC. New appendix discussion interprets sparse-compressor failures, Morton-order scalability and deployment on weaker GPUs. These substantially expand applicability and mechanism discussion. However, Appendix B's claimed Morton speedup contradicts the timing assignments in Table 9.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies lambda=2 and documents the Zip-NeRF/MCMC training budget, densification interval, feature-introduction schedule and larger SVQ codebooks. Appendix A also explains how the sparse comparator combinations were trained. Most original implementation details and the project URL are retained; the checklist additionally states that supplementary code is provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Zip-NeRF, SMERF and 3DGS-MCMC, connecting OMG to large-scene rendering and an alternative densification framework. The existing related-work taxonomy and positioning against Gaussian compression approaches remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most introductory, methodological and concluding prose is retained. Local wording is refined, the ablation discussion is reordered and rewritten in places, and a limitations section, acknowledgements and NeurIPS checklist are added. The appendix is reorganized into lettered sections; this is not a wholesale rewrite of the scientific narrative.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a single-column NeurIPS format. Figure 4 replaces its views and OMG-M/stump panels with a LocoGS comparison and enlarged crops; Figure 5 is new. Tables gain comparisons, Table 5 is substantially restructured, and the retained post-processing table is transposed. Existing appendix results are relocated and reformatted rather than removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central design choices through direct RVQ comparisons, uncompressed LD controls and sparse-compressor experiments. MCMC and Zip-NeRF evaluations, paired with explicit baseline-dependent limitations, address important gaps in v1's evidence about applicability. The new Morton/KNN timing table remains internally inconsistent: it assigns 4100 ms to OMG and 28 ms to KNN while the text claims Morton is 146 times faster. This weakens that specific conclusion, but the broader validation and clearer applicability boundaries provide a substantial net improvement.
